title: Acceptance criteria for schema negotiation, partial streaming semantics, and resilient tool-call behavior
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket codifies acceptance criteria and rollout requirements for a new structured-output contract that supports explicit schema negotiation, progressive (partial) streaming of structured results, and robust tool/function-calling behavior in the face of parse errors, backpressure, and partial failures. The goal is to enable customers to rely on a deterministic structured payload format (JSON-first), while allowing streamed partial results and well-defined error/control frames that enable resilient downstream tooling and graceful fallbacks. This PRD clarifies scope (what is in/out), enumerates required test cases, and establishes monitoring and rollout constraints.
scope_in: 1) Schema negotiation headers (version + profile) 2) Streaming JSON-Lines primary payload with control frames for progress/errors 3) Tool invocation envelope (function name, typed args) 4) Idempotency and retry tokens for partial retries 5) Backpressure / rate-limit signaling and recommended client behavior 6) Server-side validation with clear error codes and suggested recovery steps
scope_out: 1) Full client SDK implementations (SDK teams will own bindings) 2) Language-specific client examples beyond canonical JS/Python snippets 3) Non-JSON structured encodings (protobuf/etc.) in this milestone
acceptance_criteria: Schema negotiation: server and client must exchange a 'X-RI-Schema' header on initial handshake; supported values: 'ri.v1', 'ri.v1+partial' and 'ri.v1.1' (backwards compatible). When client requests an unsupported schema, server returns 415 + structured error and suggested upgrade path.

Streaming format: primary stream must be newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) with three top-level frame types: 'data' (partial structured result), 'meta' (progress/trace), and 'control' (errors/finalization). Each frame MUST include 'frame_id' (uuid), 'schema_version', and 'cursor' where applicable.

Partial results semantics: 'data' frames represent incremental, self-contained JSON subtrees that merge into the final payload. Clients must be able to apply frames idempotently using 'frame_id' and 'cursor' fields. Final 'control' frame with 'status':'complete' marks stream completion.

Tool/function call envelope: when invoking a tool, a 'control' frame with 'action':'invoke' must include 'tool_name', 'args_schema_version', and 'args' object; if args fail validation, server returns a 'control' frame with 'status':'invalid_args', canonical validation errors, and a unique 'error_token' for support/debugging.

Error modes and recovery: classify errors into 'transient' (retryable with backoff), 'client_error' (bad input/schema mismatch), and 'terminal' (incompatible configuration). Transient errors must set retry-after and provide an 'idempotency_token' for safe resume. Client errors must not be retried by server.

Backpressure and pacing: server may emit 'meta' frames with 'recommended_wait_ms' to signal client to slow input. Clients must support honoring 'recommended_wait_ms' and use exponential backoff on persistent 429/503 errors. Metrics must show <0.5% of in-flight requests relying on backpressure advice at steady-state in canary tests.

Validation and fallbacks: If client requests strict schema mode and validation fails mid-stream, the server must emit a 'control' frame with 'status':'validation_failed' and include the best-effort partial payload plus an explicit 'fallback_hint' (example: 'switch_to_plain_text' or 'call_alternate_tool').

Observability: every stream must produce traceable events (stream_start, frame_sent, frame_parsed, validation_error, stream_end). These must include trace IDs surfaced to users and appear in runtime dashboards. Acceptance: trace ID correlation must be present in corresponding log and trace within 10s of completion in dev environment.

Compatibility: New schema must be backwards-compatible with 'ri.v1' for non-streaming clients. Acceptance test must show that clients using 'ri.v1' can successfully consume server's final payload when server advertises 'ri.v1+partial' by waiting for 'status:complete'.

Security: tool invocation frames must be subject to RBAC checks; if a caller lacks permission, server returns 'control' frame 'status':'forbidden' with policy_id. Acceptance requires automated tests that assert KMS-encrypted args are never logged in plaintext in either logs or trace artifacts.
test_plan: Unit tests: validation logic for schema negotiation header, NDJSON framing, and tool-envelope parsing (coverage target 95% for new modules).

Integration tests: end-to-end harness that spins up runtime, exercises streaming partial outputs, resumes after transient failure using idempotency_token, and asserts reconstructed final payload equals expected JSON.
Load tests: 10k concurrent streams with partial frames (avg frame count 6) verifying p95 latency and <1% frame loss; run in staging with dedicated GPUs.
Canary: Gradual rollout to 5% Hosted production traffic with enriched logging and rollback window (30 minutes) before progressing to 25%/50%/100%.
Security tests: automated RBAC tests and secret-scrubbing verification against retention and logs.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge server runtime & control-frame schema changes behind feature flag. 2) Deploy to staging; run integration + load tests. 3) Canary at 5% with observability hooks enabled; hold for 24 hours of no critical errors. 4) Expand to 25% then 50% contingent on metrics. 5) Flip GA flag and publish SDK compatibility notes. Rollback triggers: >0.5% increase in customer-facing parsing errors or >2x spike in p99 latency.
decisions: Adopt NDJSON as canonical streaming payload format for this milestone to maximize client compatibility and ease of parsing.
Use explicit control frames instead of embedding meta fields in data frames to reduce ambiguity in partial-merge semantics.
Expose a minimal schema negotiation header rather than a full capability exchange to keep handshake lightweight.
open_questions: Do we need a separate binary-safe envelope for very large binary args (images/audio) in this phase? (engineering follow-up)
Should the default client behavior auto-retry on transient control frames or surface to application logic? (policy decision between UX and safety)
How do we version tool arg schemas when multiple teams publish incompatible changes? (consider centralized registry)
What SLOs should apply to partial-frame delivery vs final completion?
notes: Review feedback from design and SDK teams requested clearer merge semantics for arrays within partial frames — outcome: we require explicit 'merge_strategy' attribute per collection (append/replace/indexed). Follow-up ENG-19876 will add library helpers. Link to incident learnings: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=incident-20250123-stream-parse-failure
